script.en: Most people get stuck here. They buy another AI subscription, watch another tutorial, and still have nothing to sell. The problem is not a lack of tools. It is that 'make money with AI' is not an offer. A local business cannot buy a tool list from you. It can buy seven posts for next week's promotion. So I am setting three rules before I touch any AI: one audience, one business problem, and one delivery folder. No promise of viral reach, no promise of guaranteed sales, and no pretending the AI draft is client-ready. That constraint is what makes this experiment useful, because if the work cannot survive a simple client review, it is not a business offer yet.
script.zh: 大多数人就卡在这里。他又买一个 AI 订阅，又看一个教程，最后还是没有任何能卖的东西。问题不是工具不够，而是『用 AI 赚钱』根本不是一个服务报价。本地商家买的不是一串工具名单，而是下周活动要用的 7 张帖子。所以我在打开 AI 前先定 3 条规则：一个受众、一个生意问题、一个交付文件夹。不承诺爆款，不承诺保证成交，也不把 AI 初稿冒充客户可交付稿。这些限制才让实验有用——如果一份作品经不起简单的客户审核，它还不是生意。

script.en: Tool one is ChatGPT, but I am not asking it to 'write viral posts.' I paste a short brief: the shop sells cold brew, opens at seven, has a student discount on Tuesdays, and wants people within two miles to visit next week. Then I ask for seven post ideas in a table with five columns: hook, customer situation, one proof point, call to action, and what the owner must verify. I reject any line that invents a review, a price, or a health claim. Then I choose three ideas and ask for captions in the shop's plainspoken voice. Watch the screen: first output, red corrections, final version. The value is not the first paragraph ChatGPT gives me. The value is the repeatable brief-to-draft process and the fact that I manually check every claim before a client sees it. For the screen recording, pause after the first output and zoom in on one bad sentence. Show the prompt change, regenerate only that row, and compare the two versions side by side. That small correction is the skill a client pays for.
script.zh: 第一个工具是 ChatGPT，但我不会对它说『写 7 条爆款帖子』就结束。我先贴一份短需求：咖啡店卖冷萃，早上 7 点开门，周二有学生折扣，希望下周吸引两英里内的人到店。然后要求它用表格给出 7 个选题，列出钩子、客户场景、一个可验证信息、行动号召和老板必须核实的地方。凡是编造评价、价格或健康功效的句子全部删掉。再挑 3 条，让它改成店铺的日常口吻。屏幕上要展示：第一版、红色修改、最终版。价值不是 ChatGPT 第一段废话，而是可重复的『需求到初稿』流程，以及每个事实都人工核对。录屏时，第一版输出后暂停，放大一条有问题的句子。展示你怎么改提示词、只重新生成那一行，再把前后两版并排比较。客户真正愿意付钱的，正是这种小而明确的修改能力。

script.en: Now I move to Canva. I create one 1080-by-1080 template with the shop's two colors, one typeface, the logo in the same corner, and a reserved area for the offer. I do not generate seven random designs. I duplicate the template seven times and change only the photo, headline, and call to action. On screen, you should see me import one real product photo, remove a distracting background, adjust the headline so it is readable on a phone, and export the seven files with clean names: 01-monday-cold-brew.png through 07-sunday-reminder.png. If the design needs a stock photo, I label it. If the shop has no permission to use an image, I do not put it in the client folder. This is where the output becomes a usable asset instead of an AI mood board. I also create a tiny approval checklist beside the Canva file: logo correct, colors correct, offer correct, spelling checked, image licensed. If one box is empty, the page is not finished. The checklist prevents a pretty design from becoming an embarrassing client delivery.
script.zh: 现在打开 Canva。我先做一个 1080×1080 模板：店铺两种主色、一个字体、Logo 固定在同一角落，留出活动信息位置。我不生成 7 张随机图，而是复制模板 7 次，只替换照片、标题和 CTA。屏幕要拍到：导入一张真实产品照片、去掉干扰背景、把标题改到手机上能看清，再按 01-monday-cold-brew.png 到 07-sunday-reminder.png 规范导出。如果需要图库图，就标明来源；如果店里没有授权，就不放进交付文件夹。这里才是把 AI 草稿变成可用素材，而不是一堆灵感图。我还会在 Canva 文件旁边建一张很小的验收清单：Logo 对不对、颜色对不对、活动信息对不对、拼写检查没有、图片有授权没有。只要有一格没勾，这页就不算完成。它能防止漂亮设计变成尴尬交付。

script.en: The third tool is CapCut, and this is where I make one asset a client can actually post. I import three phone clips: pouring the cold brew, opening the shop door, and a close-up of the finished cup. I cut the first second so the cup appears immediately, add on-screen text that matches the offer, generate captions, and remove any sentence the auto-caption tool gets wrong. Then I export a thirty-second vertical video and check it on my phone with the sound off. The failure point is important: AI can assemble a video, but it cannot know whether the product name, price, or opening hours are correct. I keep the project file, the MP4, and a plain text caption together. That is the difference between demonstrating a tool and demonstrating a deliverable. Before exporting, I show the raw clip, the timeline, the caption correction, and the final phone preview as four separate cuts. That lets the audience verify the transformation instead of trusting a polished montage. It also tells a future client exactly what they are buying: edited media, not an AI button.
script.zh: 第三个工具是 CapCut，我要做出一个客户真能发布的素材。我导入 3 段手机视频：倒冷萃、推开店门、成品杯特写。第一秒就让杯子出现，加入和活动一致的屏幕文字，生成字幕，再把自动字幕里错的句子全部改掉。导出 30 秒竖屏视频后，用手机静音检查一遍。这里的失败点很重要：AI 可以帮你拼视频，但不知道商品名、价格和营业时间是不是正确。我把工程文件、MP4 和纯文本文案放在一起交付。这就是『演示工具』和『演示交付物』的区别。导出前，我会把原始素材、时间线、字幕纠错和手机最终预览剪成 4 个独立镜头。观众能验证素材怎样变成成品，而不是只相信一段精修混剪。对未来客户来说也很清楚：他买的是编辑后的媒体文件，不是一个 AI 按钮。

script.en: Here is the part most 'make money with AI' videos skip: the offer and the math. My time log says fifteen minutes for the brief, thirty-five for the captions, fifty-five for the Canva set, forty-five for the short video, and twenty minutes for quality control. That is two hours and fifty minutes before revisions. At a $100 price, the gross rate is about $35 an hour before software, taxes, and a second revision. So I would write the offer narrowly: one round of revisions, client supplies the logo and approved photos, delivery in three days, no promise of followers or sales. If the client wants five videos and daily posting, that is a different price. The experiment earns credibility because I show the boundary, not because I wave a fake income screenshot. I would also put a revision counter on the sheet. If the first revision takes another ninety minutes, the original $100 offer is no longer the same job. That is the moment to reduce the scope, raise the price, or stop. Showing that decision protects the audience from copying a fantasy hourly rate.
script.zh: 这是大多数『AI 赚钱』视频跳过的部分：报价和算账。我的时间表是：需求单 15 分钟，文案 35 分钟，Canva 套图 55 分钟，短视频 45 分钟，质检 20 分钟。还没算修改，就已经 2 小时 50 分。报价 100 美元，毛时薪大约 35 美元，还要扣软件、税和第二轮修改。所以我的报价必须写窄：包含 1 轮修改，客户提供 Logo 和已授权照片，3 天交付，不承诺涨粉或成交。如果客户要 5 条视频和每天代发，那是另一档价格。这个实验可信，不是因为我甩一张假的收入截图，而是因为我把边界和成本都展示出来。我还会在表格里加一列修改次数。如果第一轮修改又花了 90 分钟，原来的 100 美元就已经不是同一份工作了。这时要么缩小范围、要么提高报价、要么停止。把这个决定展示出来，才能防止观众照抄一个幻想中的时薪。

script.en: The line to remember is simple: do not sell 'AI.' Sell a finished file that removes a specific task from someone's week. packages.hook: Before you invest another dollar, open your credit-card statement. If the APR is 22% and your realistic long-term after-inflation return assumption is 7%, I can show you in under two minutes why the order matters — and the one 401(k) exception that changes the answer.
packages.hook_zh: 在你再投一美元之前，先打开信用卡账单。如果 APR 是 22%，而你对长期扣除通胀后的投资回报只按 7% 做保守假设，我用不到两分钟算给你看为什么顺序重要，以及唯一会改变答案的 401(k) 例外。

hook_options.label: 戳中『一边投资一边被利息吸血』
hook_options.en: If your brokerage balance is going up but your credit-card balance is growing faster, you are not getting ahead. You are watching one account climb while another account charges you 22% for the privilege. Open your statement — we are going to run your numbers, not mine.
hook_options.zh: 如果你的券商账户在涨，但信用卡债涨得更快，你并没有变富。你只是看着一个账户往上走，同时让另一个账户收你 22% 的利息。打开你的账单，我们算你的数字，不算我的。

hook_options.label: 打破『永远先投资』
hook_options.en: 'Invest first, always' is incomplete advice. A 401(k) match can come first. A 22% credit-card balance usually should not. I will put both rules on one decision tree and show you exactly where the answer changes.
hook_options.zh: 『永远先投资』是一句不完整的建议。401(k) 的公司配比可以优先，但 22% 的信用卡债通常不该优先投资。我把两条规则放进一张决策树，现场告诉你答案在哪一步改变。

hook_options.label: 90 秒三问测试 + 三个案例
hook_options.en: Give me ninety seconds and three numbers: your APR, your monthly extra cash, and your employer match. I will show you which line to follow, what to type into a payoff calculator, and which mistake can cost you thousands over time.
hook_options.zh: 给我 90 秒和 3 个数字：你的 APR、每月能多拿出的现金、以及公司 401(k) 配比。我会告诉你该走哪条线、还款计算器里怎么填，以及哪个错误可能让你长期多付几千美元。

script.en: Here is why this question feels so confusing. Your investment account gives you a green number every time the market rises, while your credit-card statement hides the cost in a minimum payment. Suppose the balance is $8,000 and the APR is 22%. A rough annual interest charge is about $1,760 before the balance changes. Now compare that with a 7% long-term after-inflation assumption on $8,000: about $560 in expected growth, not guaranteed, and possibly negative in a bad year. The emotional mistake is treating those two numbers as if they have the same certainty. They do not. Paying down the card removes a known cost. Investing accepts an uncertain result. That does not mean every debt must be paid before every investment. It means you need to compare the rate, the tax treatment, the time horizon, and the employer match instead of repeating 'invest first' or 'pay debt first' for everyone.
script.zh: 这个问题让人困惑，是因为投资账户在市场上涨时每次都给你一个绿色上涨数字，而信用卡账单把成本藏在最低还款额里。假设欠 8,000 美元、APR 22%，粗略算一年利息约 1,760 美元，先不考虑余额变化。再看 8,000 美元按长期扣除通胀后 7% 的假设，大约是 560 美元的预期增长，不是保证，坏年份还可能是负数。真正的心理错误，是把这两个数字当成同样确定。它们不是一回事。还卡是在消除已知成本，投资是在接受不确定结果。这不代表所有债务都必须排在所有投资前，而是你要比较利率、税务、时间期限和雇主配比，不要对所有人重复『先投资』或『先还债』。

script.en: Now open the source instead of trusting a thumbnail. On the Federal Reserve G.19 page, show the difference between the average rate across all credit-card accounts and the rate on accounts assessed interest. Use the assessed-interest figure only as a current reference for people carrying a balance, and put the publication date on screen. Then open Investor.gov's compound-interest calculator. Enter a sample starting balance, a monthly contribution, a conservative return assumption, and a five-year period. Do not type 'the market returns 10%' as if it were a promise. The viewer should see four boxes: starting balance, monthly contribution, assumed return, and years. Screenshot the input and result. That is the moment your video becomes verifiable: anyone can replace your sample numbers with their own and reproduce the calculation.
script.zh: 现在打开来源页面，不要相信缩略图。在 Federal Reserve 的 G.19 页面里，展示『全部信用卡账户平均利率』和『正在计息账户利率』的区别。对真正背着余额的人，只把计息账户数字当当前参考，并把发布日期放在画面上。然后打开 Investor.gov 的复利计算器，输入示例初始金额、每月投入、保守回报假设和 5 年期限。不要把『市场回报 10%』写得像保证。让观众看到 4 个输入框：初始金额、每月投入、假设回报、年数。截下输入和结果。这样视频才可验证：任何人都能替换示例数字，复算一遍。

script.en: Let's run three households. Case A has $8,000 on a 22% card and $500 a month. In the payoff calculator, enter the balance, APR, and payment, then record months to payoff and total interest. Case B has the same $500 but a 7% loan, so we compare the payoff schedule with investing the same monthly amount. Case C has a 3.5% mortgage, where the spread is much smaller and liquidity may matter more. The point is not that one calculator can predict the future. The point is that the viewer can see the decision variables. On screen, keep a table with APR, payment, payoff date, interest, assumed investment return, and ending balance. Never hide the assumptions in narration. If the answer changes when you move from 22% to 7%, that change is the lesson. For the video, I would click the calculator result open, not just flash a final number. First show the 22% case, then change only the APR to 7%, then change it to 3.5%. Keeping the balance and payment visible makes the comparison fair and teaches the audience which variable is doing the work.
script.zh: 我们跑 3 个家庭。案例 A：8,000 美元、22% 信用卡债，每月 500 美元。在还款计算器里输入余额、APR 和月供，记录多久还清、总利息多少。案例 B：同样每月 500 美元，但债务利率是 7%，把还款计划和把同样金额拿去投资放在一起比较。案例 C：3.5% 房贷，利差更小，流动性可能更重要。重点不是某个计算器能预测未来，而是让观众看到决策变量。屏幕上保留一张表：APR、月供、还清日期、利息、投资回报假设和期末余额。不要把假设藏在旁白里。如果从 22% 换成 7% 后答案发生变化，这个变化本身就是知识点。拍视频时，我会把计算器结果完整展开，而不是只闪过最后一个数字。先展示 22% 案例，再只把 APR 改成 7%，最后改成 3.5%。余额和月供始终留在画面里，比较才公平，观众也能看出究竟是哪一个变量改变了结果。

script.en: Three traps make otherwise smart people ignore the result. Trap one is a 0% promotional APR. Open the offer and show the expiration date, balance-transfer fee, and regular APR after the promotion. Trap two is 'I'll invest the gains and use them to pay the card.' Put the two rates side by side and label the market return expected, not guaranteed. Trap three is keeping a giant emergency fund in a low-yield account while the card compounds at a much higher rate. Do not tell the viewer to empty their cash. Show a conservative rule: keep a basic cash buffer, then compare the yield on excess cash with the card APR. The practical shot is the important shot: highlight the exact field in the statement or offer that changes the calculation. A trap is useful only when viewers know where to look. Put a red box around each trap and a green box around the field that must be checked. For a promotional card, the audience should be able to pause and find the end date. For savings, they should see APY. For debt, they should see APR. A useful finance video teaches the viewer how to inspect a document.
script.zh: 三个坑会让聪明人忽略结果。第一个是 0% 促销 APR。打开 offer，展示结束日期、转账手续费，以及促销结束后的常规 APR。第二个是『我先投资，拿收益来还卡』。把两个利率并排，给市场回报标上『预期，不保证』。第三个是把大额应急金放在低收益账户里，而信用卡以高得多的利率复利。不要告诉观众把现金全部拿走，而是展示一个保守规则：先留基本现金缓冲，再把多余现金的存款收益和信用卡 APR 放在一起比较。实操画面最重要：把账单或 offer 上真正改变计算的字段圈出来。一个陷阱只有在观众知道该看哪里时，才有用。每个陷阱用红框，必须核对的字段用绿框。促销卡要让观众暂停后找到结束日期；储蓄账户要找到 APY；债务账单要找到 APR。真正有用的财经视频，教观众怎么读一份文件，而不只是告诉观众一个结论。
script.viz: 依次打开 0% offer、账单和储蓄账户页面，圈出 expiration / fee / regular APR / APY

demo.proof: 观众学会读文件，而不是只记住『0% 有坑』。

script.en: Now the exception that can override the debt rule: an employer 401(k) match. Open a sample pay stub or plan document and find the exact match formula. If the plan matches 50 cents for every dollar you contribute up to 6% of pay, contributing enough to capture the full match can create an immediate employer contribution. The screen should show the formula, not just a gold-coin animation. Then draw the order: minimum cash buffer, capture the full match, attack high-interest debt, handle lower-rate debt according to the spread and your risk, then invest the remaining money. If your plan has vesting rules, fees, or a different match formula, show those too. This is not a universal prescription. It is a checklist for reading your own plan before making a decision. If the plan document is unclear, the correct on-camera move is to stop and say so, then tell viewers to call the plan administrator. Never fill the blank with a guessed match formula. The credibility moment is admitting that a personal plan can differ from the example.
script.zh: 现在讲唯一可能推翻高息债规则的例外：公司 401(k) 配比。打开一张示例工资单或计划文件，找到准确的配比公式。如果公司是你缴工资 6% 以内的每 1 美元配 0.5 美元，那么缴到拿满配比，就会收到一笔即时的公司缴款。画面要展示公式，不要只放金币动画。然后画出顺序：基本现金缓冲 → 拿满配比 → 攻击高息债 → 根据利差和风险处理低息债 → 把剩余资金拿去投资。如果计划有归属期、费用或不同配比公式，也要展示。这里不是给所有人一条处方，而是教你在做决定前先读懂自己的计划文件。如果计划文件写得不清楚，镜头前正确的做法是停下来说明，然后告诉观众联系计划管理员。不要猜一个配比公式填空。真正建立可信度的时刻，是承认每个人的计划都可能和示例不同。
script.viz: 屏幕录制计划文件中的 match formula，白板画出 match → high APR debt → low APR debt → invest

steps: 打开 plan document
找到 employer match 章节

demo.proof: 观众知道『先拿免费钱』不是口号，而是读自己的计划文件。

script.en: Here is the sentence to remember: paying off a high-interest balance is not anti-investing — it is removing a known drag before you take an uncertain risk. Tonight, write down your APR, your monthly extra cash, and your employer match. Put them into the three-question sheet, open the official source links, and save the assumptions next to the result. Do not copy my example as personal advice. If you want the next calculator walkthrough, comment with the word MATH. Subscribe, because next week I will show how to choose which card to attack when you have three balances and only one extra payment. The goal is not a louder opinion. It is a decision you can reproduce.
script.zh: 记住这句话：还清高息债不是反对投资，而是在承担不确定风险之前，先移除一个确定的拖累。今晚写下你的 APR、每月额外现金和公司配比，把它们填进三问表，打开官方来源链接，并把假设和结果放在一起保存。不要把我的示例当成对你的个人建议。如果你想看下一期计算器实操，评论区打 MATH。订阅频道，下周我展示同时有 3 张卡、每月只能多还一张时，到底先攻哪张。目标不是更响亮的观点，而是一套你能自己复算的决定。

packages.description: 先还债还是先投资？本视频按用户自己的三组数字现场演示：APR、每月额外现金、雇主 401(k) 配比。通过 Federal Reserve G.19、Investor.gov 复利计算器、债务还款计算器和三个示例场景，区分确定的利息节省与不确定的市场回报；再演示 0% 促销、转账费、应急金和 401(k) match 这些会改变答案的字段。示例仅用于教育演示，不构成个别投资建议；发布前回官方来源核对最新数据、日期、利率和个人计划条款。
